look_here_first: Crush-free visual ID starts with the tiny narrow leaves: damianita is a low woody-based subshrub with many very narrow aromatic gland-dotted leaves and solitary bright-yellow heads held above the canopy on slender peduncles.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: evergreen aromatic subshrub with woody lower stems; many short linear to linear-oblanceolate leaves; leaves conspicuously oil-gland dotted under magnification; solitary terminal radiate heads on slender peduncles; bright yellow ray florets surrounding yellow disc florets; involucre with relatively few phyllaries and conspicuous oil glands; pappus of many capillary bristles; inferior ovary maturing into a cypsela

key_traits.label: Family training
key_traits.text: Good Asteraceae whole-plant-to-head lesson: aromatic/gland-dotted narrow foliage gets you close, then involucre, ray/disc florets and cypsela/pappus confirm the composite structure.

key_traits.label: Video training
key_traits.text: Joey shows the whole plant and flower heads in thin limestone habitat and mentions aromatic foliage and Tageteae.

lookalikes.differences: Damianita is a low woody-based aromatic subshrub with numerous tiny linear gland-dotted leaves; Tetraneuris linearifolia is an annual herb with a different involucre/pappus pattern.
